clue.text: It's polite to provide notes fore arrival

indicators.note: fore means in front, so the notes are placed ahead of the word for arrival

blocks.note: two musical notes, B and E
an arrival is a coming

explanation.surface: A point of etiquette: it is good manners to send a note before you turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore' is a pun on 'before', telling you the notes come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming as an adjective means fitting or seemly, close to courteous and proper in behaviour.

clue.text: Quail, hair having lost its colour

blocks.note: a bob is a short haircut
hair that has lost its colour has gone white

explanation.surface: Someone recoils in fear and their hair turns white with shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like a verb meaning cower; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobwhite is a North American game bird of the quail family, named for its call.

clue.text: Land of luxury, sounds addictive

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by what a word is heard as, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: cocaine is a notoriously addictive drug

explanation.surface: A life of luxury is described as habit-forming.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockaigne is the imaginary medieval paradise of idleness and plenty where food and comfort abound.

clue.text: Painter is late rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: ten a.m. is a late hour to get up, so 'late rising' suggests that time

explanation.surface: An artist is said to be a late riser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' works twice: ten a.m. is a late rising time, and the letters of TEN AM written upwards give the French painter MANET.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French artist, forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Joshua's dad embraces the Egyptian Queen - there's strong attraction here

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one name wraps around the other

blocks.note: in the Bible Joshua is the son of Nun
short for Cleopatra, queen of Egypt

explanation.surface: A biblical father hugs Cleopatra, and there is clearly chemistry between them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'strong attraction' sounds romantic but is the strong nuclear force that binds particles in an atom's nucleus.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, held in the atomic nucleus by the strong force.

clue.text: Schoolboy fetched a sort of rissole

blocks.note: at British public schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior
to fetch something is to go and get it

explanation.surface: A boy at school was sent to collect some fried meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A FAG fetching things for older boys fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A faggot is a British meatball of offal and breadcrumbs, a kind of rissole served with gravy.

clue.text: As a group, move to imprison leader of European court

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so these letters are rearranged
a prison holds someone inside, so one letter goes within the others
the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: A collective decision to lock up the head of a European court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Areopagus was the ancient Athenian high court, meeting on the hill of Ares.

clue.text: You have to follow up character who never appeared

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to chase up someone who failed to show.
explanation.walkthrough: TO DOG written upwards gives GODOT; 'You have to' also hints at the endless waiting in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot the title figure is awaited throughout but never arrives on stage.

clue.text: Cheap metal trophy is worthless

blocks.note: tin is a cheap common metal
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: A cheap metal cup is judged to be of no value.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means shoddy, inferior or of little account, as in a tinpot dictator.

clue.text: Make the top, using rope

blocks.note: first meaning: a sleeveless top fastened behind the neck
second meaning: a rope or strap for leading a horse

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a garment out of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rope top; the word is both the garment and the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is both a strappy garment tied at the neck and a headstall rope for leading animals.

clue.text: St Albans embargo holds firm

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A trade ban stays in place in the Hertfordshire city of St Albans.
explanation.walkthrough: St Albans looks like the city; it is Francis Bacon, who was made Viscount St Alban.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher Francis Bacon held the title Viscount St Alban, so the name stands for the man.

clue.text: Girl has a new fellow, a historian

blocks.note: a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for new
a fellow of a college is a don

explanation.surface: A young woman has a new boyfriend who studies history.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hyde, Earl of Clarendon, wrote a famous history of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Breathe out, at last showing a sign of life

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
last tells us where to put the short word: at the very end

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient finally exhales, proving they are still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally' but means put AT last.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse or beating heart is the standard check that a person is still alive.

clue.text: Aim for the hole: O boy, what a beauty!

blocks.note: in golf a putt is a stroke aimed at the hole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer lines up a putt and the onlooker exclaims at a lovely shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O boy, what a beauty!' sounds like a commentator's cry; split it to get the letter O and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a chubby cherub-like infant figure in Renaissance and Baroque art, often beautiful.

clue.text: Don't relax, having drunk a measure

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
an en is a printer's measure

explanation.surface: Someone is warned to stay alert after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten is to make taut or stricter, the opposite of slackening or easing off.

clue.text: Wader sets course for Northumberland

blocks.note: a ship that sets course for a place turns to it
Northumberland is a county in north-east England, NE

explanation.surface: A wading bird heads off towards the far north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a shore bird that flips stones over on beaches to find food.

clue.text: Rough indulged in horseplay

blocks.note: first meaning: tattered, uneven
second meaning: teased or played rough pranks

explanation.surface: Someone played roughly in boisterous fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged as an adjective means torn or jagged; as a past tense verb it means teased or fooled about.

clue.text: Able to walk and talk: tell me more!

indicators.note: something made to walk wanders about, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
to orate is to give a speech

explanation.surface: A toddler who can walk and talk is urged to keep chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to elaborate is asking them to expand with more detail.

clue.text: Throw out demand of the French to be inside annexe

indicators.note: something thrown out is scattered, so these letters are rearranged
inside tells us one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a French demand to be housed in an extra building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annexe' suggests a building, but here it is a section added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material appended to a book or document, just as an annexe is.

clue.text: Boy finally obtains desires

indicators.note: finally points at the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: its last letter
to earn is to obtain by work

explanation.surface: A lad at last gets what he wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something deeply, so it is a verb meaning wants.

clue.text: Allure concealed by monotonous fabric

indicators.note: what is concealed is hidden inside something else, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: monotonous things are all the same
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Charm is lost in a dull, dreary cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk cloth, often woven with gold, worn in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Is to phone back on the motorway when lost

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left
in an across clue, on places one piece after another

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
taken as written
to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: A driver who is lost on the motorway is told to ring back.
explanation.definitionFit: Mislaid means put somewhere and forgotten, so the thing is lost for now.

clue.text: Ferdinand's girl gets letters from Irma

indicators.note: taking a name's letters frees them to be put in any order
gets says the girl obtains only a piece of the preceding name, its tail end, with the rest dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
only its final three letters are kept

explanation.surface: Ferdinand's girlfriend is sent letters by a woman called Irma.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest Ferdinand falls for MIRANDA, Prospero's daughter; the AND at the end of his name joins Irma's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a girl's name, and the heroine of The Tempest whom Ferdinand loves.

clue.text: Spirit declared to customs by Wilde

blocks.note: first meaning: a guardian spirit
second meaning: Oscar Wilde reputedly told US customs he had nothing to declare except this

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde declares some alcohol at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' at customs suggests liquor; it is the guardian spirit sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman belief a genius was a person's guardian spirit, and Wilde famously declared his own brilliance.

clue.text: Bell island?

blocks.note: first meaning: Emily Brontë wrote as ... Bell
second meaning: the New York island where immigrants were processed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like a common noun; it is the surname in Emily Brontë's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Bell was Emily Brontë's pseudonym, and Ellis Island was the immigration station in New York harbour.

clue.text: Time for some Schubert

blocks.note: surface reading: a moment to put on some Schubert
setter's reading: the word that comes before 'Time' in the title of an operetta built on Schubert's melodies

explanation.walkthrough: Lilac Time is a 1922 London operetta arranged from Schubert's music, so the word is what goes 'for' Time.
explanation.definitionFit: The operetta Lilac Time, adapted from Das Dreimäderlhaus, uses Schubert's tunes throughout.

clue.text: How the Walrus kept secrets from the Carpenter?

definitions.text: How the Walrus kept secrets from the Carpenter?

blocks.clueFragment: How the Walrus kept secrets from the Carpenter?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter
setter's reading: morse is an old word for a walrus, so its cipher would be named after it

explanation.walkthrough: Morse is an old name for the walrus, so the walrus's secret cipher is punningly the telegraph code.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse's system of dots and dashes is a code for sending messages.

clue.text: Quadruped from the Orient?

blocks.note: surface reading: an animal native to Asia
setter's reading: the East, written E, followed by a word for a country

explanation.walkthrough: The animal is African, so the question mark warns that 'from the Orient' is a pun: E for east plus land.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, a four-legged grazing animal.

clue.text: I will proceed to get clear return, by illegal means

definitions.note: adverbial phrase for an adjective meaning obtained this way

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: I'll is the short form
to go is to proceed
to net or nett is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: Someone plans to pocket a clear profit through crooked dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten describes gains acquired dishonestly or unlawfully.

clue.text: Decoration of some beds

blocks.note: a single unspecified one
a hospital ward is a room of beds

explanation.surface: Ornaments on some flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests a garden; it is a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal or honour given for merit is both an award and a decoration.

clue.text: Make a packet out of a way to inhibit pain

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in check, so one word is held within another

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone profits from a method of pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a packet' reads as get rich; only 'packet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag or envelope holding a single portion.

clue.text: May dread being upset, but it's not likely to happen really

definitions.text: it's not likely to happen really

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: May worries about something that is unlikely to come about.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a fanciful reverie about things that are not going to come true.
